subject: kraken
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: kraken rising, tentacles spread.
Style: Overwatch.
reasoning:
I'm designing a kraken with a bulbous mantle head, big eyes, a beak, and eight tentacles spreading outward in a rising pose, using a bold stylized Overwatch-like aesthetic with clean shapes and glowing accents.

Planning the joint hierarchy now: a core root, a spine chain swept upward and back to form the bulbous body, and the front-facing eyes placed as decaled spheres on the mantle surface.

For placement, I'll use the nearest-surface-point method instead of raycasting so I always get a valid hit for decals, which avoids null-hit errors. I'm also sketching out the beak as upper and lower cones attached to a jaw joint mounted near the front-bottom of the body, using the same nearest-surface trick to anchor it correctly.

Now I'm setting up a joint hierarchy: a head joint off the spine parenting the jaw, with eyes and brow parts defaulting to whichever joint is closest. Next I'm planning the tentacles—eight of them spaced evenly in azimuth around a ring at the body's base.

For each tentacle I'm defining a curved path from root outward and down to the floor, mixing some that rise and curl high with others that lie spread along the ground, making sure every point stays above floor level relative to its tube radius so nothing clips through.

Checking floor sink tolerance looks fine, then I'm setting up each tentacle as a chain built from Catmull-Rom points, parented to the core joint alongside the spine chain, and defining sweep paint sectors for the underside suckers coloring.

For the color palette I'm going with a deep indigo-purple skin countershaded against a coral belly, with cyan glow accent spots, and planning sucker placement along the tentacle's belly-facing side using the sweep's parametric position.

I'm adding belly suckers via small cylinders placed along each tentacle's underside, plus glowing orb spots on the back and spike cones near the top — keeping the total part count manageable around a couple hundred pieces.

Now I'm thinking about fins and a dorsal crest: considering side fins extruded as a leaf shape versus a simpler spine of spikes running along the top of the mantle using the body sweep points, settling on the spike approach since it's easier to size and position consistently.

Still working out fin orientation...

For the eyes, I need to place them by raycasting against the body's spine curve and radius profile, since the mantle leans back with varying thickness along its length.

I'm planning an elliptical eye decal with a yellow iris, black slit pupil, highlights, dark outline, and a dark purple upper lid, plus a small angled brow piece above each eye for an angry expression.

For the beak, I'm positioning it near the front of the body using a nearest-surface hit and shaping the upper part as a short downward-pointing cone.

Still defining jaw and beak joints...

Now I'm thinking about adding glowing cyan emblem decals on the mantle's upper back, placing symmetric rune-like rings and dots on either side as a decorative accent.

I'll also add a small glowing sphere at each tentacle's tip, finding the end joint of each chain and dropping a glow-enabled cyan sphere there. I decide to skip the idea of a rising water ring since nothing explicitly calls for it, and move on to paint: countershading the body with mottled indigo-violet tones fading to coral on the belly, plus cyan spot patterns layered onto the back.

For the spots I'll use a brighter cyan hex with modest size and sparse coverage so they read like glowing accents, restricting them to the top of the body via the countershade belly mask. For the tentacles, I'm reusing the same base coat and adding pink belly-strip sectors, deciding to skip trying to blend sectors into banded tip colors and just rely on the glowing sphere for that highlight instead.

Now I'm sizing the body sweep radii per spine joint and checking whether to widen the sweep sides for smoother shading, leaning toward keeping it simple with default smoothing. I'm also checking where the tentacle root sits relative to the body radius, confirming it starts just inside the body surface so the joint blends cleanly rather than poking out.

Thinking through the tentacle placement, I'm spacing them evenly around the body using an azimuth angle offset by 22.5 degrees, alternating between two tentacle shapes for variety, and adding slight random scale variation so they don't look identical.

Writing tentacle curve math...

Planning spikes along sweep points at specific t-values for a horned texture, then thinking through sucker geometry as layered cylinders—a pale pink outer ring with a darker inner cylinder for the detail.

Adding angry eyelid shapes...

Adding the glowing rune decal with cyan SVG lines, then working out fin placement and outline shapes that flare up and outward like ears from the body surface.

I'm giving the fins an orange "#ff8a3d" tone to pop against the cyan trim, layering a smaller darker rim extrude for depth, and wrapping it into a reusable fin(sc, thick, color) helper. Then I move to beak details, building the upper beak as a flat five-sided cone oriented along a direction vector.

Working out positioning: I'm placing the upper beak's base so it nestles slightly into the body surface, and setting the lower jaw cone at an offset below with its own tilt direction and size, finishing with a darker mouth interior.

I also want to scatter small barnacle-like cones across the back using a surface scatter filtered to upward-facing normals, and I'm checking the lowest tentacle points to make sure they touch or sink into the floor properly.

Finishing up the taper calculations...
